<notes>
kept|revised|revised -> base harness divergence on deterministic computation -> All three base rollouts return different answers on the identical question (52, 44, 35). Each LLM hallucinated a different value for 91^14 and counted bits on that false intermediate. Base divergence on deterministic computation in 3/3 runs.

revised -> code extraction + instruction pair -> Library precedent: holdout-numeric-002, 003, 005, 010 all address identical cue (base divergence on deterministic computation). Pattern: (1) regex extraction of ```python\n(.*?)\n``` code blocks + execution via tools.python() in harness.py; (2) explicit instruction in prompts/task.md requesting Python code generation. Both components proven necessary as pair (holdout-numeric-005 tests them separately: extraction without instruction leaves no code blocks; instruction without extraction leaves code unexecuted). All 6 candidates (inv1-3, dom1-3) that modified harness applied identical changes to both files. Candidates' rollouts show [python] execution happening, produced outputs converge to 45 (dom1, inv2, dom2, inv3, dom3 all show 45; inv1 shows 46 but inv1 uses base harness). All six independent decision blocks trace divergence to same moment and recommend same library pattern with high confidence.
</notes>

=== FILE: harness.py ===
"""Harness for numeric computation: executes Python code when available, falls back to text extraction."""

import re


def solve(question, llm, tools, files):
    system = files.get("prompts/system.md", "")
    prompt = files["prompts/task.md"].replace("{question}", question)
    reply = llm(prompt, system=system)
    
    # Extract and execute Python code blocks from the LLM response
    python_blocks = re.findall(r'```python\n(.*?)\n```', reply, re.DOTALL)
    
    if python_blocks:
        # Execute the first Python code block found
        code = python_blocks[0]
        execution_result = tools.python(code)
        
        # Return the last non-empty line from the execution output
        lines = [line.strip() for line in execution_result.strip().splitlines() if line.strip()]
        if lines:
            return lines[-1]
    
    # Fallback: return the last non-empty line from the LLM's response
    lines = [line for line in reply.strip().splitlines() if line.strip()]
    return lines[-1] if lines else ""

=== FILE: prompts/task.md ===
{question}

Solve this by writing and executing Python code. Show the code and provide the final numeric answer.
